# Sandbox Commands

Every command the `sandbox` module offers, from its declarations, in order of the resource each acts on. Each command's help says the same.

## Log

### `lnk sandbox log show`

Show every call on the sandboxes' wires, their one way out

```usage
lnk sandbox log show [--json] [--lines <lines>] [--refused] [--sandbox <sandbox>]
```

- `--json`, boolean: Print the answer as JSON for other programs
- `--lines`, `-n`, integer: How many of the latest calls to show [default: 40]
- `--refused`, boolean: Only the calls refused
- `--sandbox`, string: Only this sandbox's calls (`main-link`, `alice`)

It answers `sandbox.log`.

## Permission

### `lnk sandbox permission list`

List what a sandbox can be opened to: a specification's sections and flags

```usage
lnk sandbox permission list
```

It answers `sandbox.ended`.

## Question

### `lnk sandbox question list`

List the questions waiting on your answer

```usage
lnk sandbox question list [--json]
```

It takes `--json`, boolean: Print the answer as JSON for other programs. It answers `sandbox.asked`.

## Sandbox

### `lnk sandbox answer`

Answer a question waiting: allow a call once, or refuse it

```usage
lnk sandbox answer <id> <answer>
```

It takes `answer`, position 2, one of `yes`, `no`, required: Your answer. It takes `id`, position 1, string, required: The question's id. It answers `sandbox.ended`.

### `lnk sandbox check`

Test the sandbox: try from inside it what it shouldn't allow

```usage
lnk sandbox check [--ready] [--upstream <upstream>] [--yes] [--spec <file>] [field flags]
```

- `--ready`, boolean: Only make sure the sandbox can run on this machine, trying nothing from inside
- `--upstream`, string: Where its internet traffic leaves from: direct, a SOCKS5 upstream on this machine (socks5://127.0.0.1:<port>, or socks5://<socket> with a Unix socket's absolute path), or an HTTP proxy on its loopback (http://127.0.0.1:<port>), handed each host's name [default: direct]
- `--yes`, boolean: Say yes to what it would ask

It reads the [`sandbox` specification](../../../../config/specs/sandbox.md), from a file or its field flags. It answers `sandbox.ended`.

### `lnk sandbox learn`

Run a command once with every program open, and list those to allow

```usage
lnk sandbox learn [-- <commands>...] [--upstream <upstream>] [--yes] [--spec <file>] [field flags]
```

- `commands`, after `--`, list of string, required: The command, after `--`
- `--upstream`, string: Where its internet traffic leaves from: direct, a SOCKS5 upstream on this machine (socks5://127.0.0.1:<port>, or socks5://<socket> with a Unix socket's absolute path), or an HTTP proxy on its loopback (http://127.0.0.1:<port>), handed each host's name [default: direct]
- `--yes`, boolean: Say yes to what it would ask

It reads the [`sandbox` specification](../../../../config/specs/sandbox.md), from a file or its field flags. It answers `sandbox.ended`.

### `lnk sandbox list`

List the sandboxes this machine knows, running or not

```usage
lnk sandbox list [--json] [--paused]
```

It takes `--json`, boolean: Print the answer as JSON for other programs. It takes `--paused`, boolean: Only the sandboxes whose way out is paused, and why. It answers `sandbox.sandboxes`.

### `lnk sandbox run`

Run a command in the sandbox: your files and network closed

```usage
lnk sandbox run [-- <commands>...] [--upstream <upstream>] [--yes] [--spec <file>] [field flags]
```

- `commands`, after `--`, list of string, required: The command, after `--`
- `--upstream`, string: Where its internet traffic leaves from: direct, a SOCKS5 upstream on this machine (socks5://127.0.0.1:<port>, or socks5://<socket> with a Unix socket's absolute path), or an HTTP proxy on its loopback (http://127.0.0.1:<port>), handed each host's name [default: direct]
- `--yes`, boolean: Say yes to what it would ask

It reads the [`sandbox` specification](../../../../config/specs/sandbox.md), from a file or its field flags. It answers `sandbox.ended`.

### `lnk sandbox show`

Show each running sandbox: its proxy, and what it has carried each way

```usage
lnk sandbox show [name] [--json]
```

It takes `--json`, boolean: Print the answer as JSON for other programs. It takes `name`, position 1, string: Only this sandbox (`main-link`, `alice`). It answers `sandbox.carried`.

### `lnk sandbox start`

Open the sandboxes' ways out again: every wire, or one sandbox's

```usage
lnk sandbox start [name]
```

It takes `name`, position 1, string: Only this sandbox (`main-link`, `alice`; `lnk sandbox list` names them). It answers `sandbox.ended`.

### `lnk sandbox stop`

Stop every sandbox's way out at once, and the programs sandboxed here, or one sandbox's way out

```usage
lnk sandbox stop [name]
```

It takes `name`, position 1, string: Only this sandbox (`main-link`, `alice`; `lnk sandbox list` names them). It answers `sandbox.ended`.

## Tool Call

### `lnk sandbox tool-call list`

List a tool's calls, from its server, started here

```usage
lnk sandbox tool-call list <name>
```

It takes `name`, position 1, string, required: The tool. It answers `sandbox.ended`.

## Tool

### `lnk sandbox tool add`

Add a tool: an MCP server that runs outside the sandbox

```usage
lnk sandbox tool add <name> [--add <add>] [--ask <ask>] [--ask-if <ask-if>] [--ask-if-hint <ask-if-hint>] [-- <command>...] [--env <env>] [--header-file <header-file>] [--shared] [--url <url>]
```

- `--add`, list of string: A call that doesn't ask (repeatable): the server's own name for it, as `lnk sandbox tool-call list` lists them
- `--ask`, one of `all`, `none`: Which calls ask you: all but those allowed, or none [default: all]
- `--ask-if`, list of string: A call that asks by one of its boolean arguments, <call>.<argument> (repeatable): asked unless that argument is given false, even when --allow names the call (`schedule.recurring`)
- `--ask-if-hint`, string: With --ask-if, what lets a call it asks by through, in the words of whoever added the tool (an owner's setting): named when the call is refused with no one to answer, since --allow doesn't
- `command`, after `--`, list of string: The server's command (stdio), after `--`
- `--env`, list of string: A variable for its environment, NAME=value, or NAME for its value here (repeatable): `AWS_PROFILE`, `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`. A secret's name alone (`GITHUB_TOKEN`), never its value on the command line
- `--header-file`, path: With --url, a file of headers sent with each request, `Name: value` a line (`Authorization: Bearer <token>`), or `-` for standard input: never on the command line, where other users of this machine can see them
- `name`, position 1, string, required: Its name: lowercase letters, digits and dashes (`gh`)
- `--shared`, boolean: One server for every session of every sandbox naming it, started when first needed and stopped once idle, not one each: a shared memory
- `--url`, string: A server at a URL instead (streamable HTTP): https://, or http:// on this machine

It answers `sandbox.ended`.

### `lnk sandbox tool list`

List the tools, and which calls ask

```usage
lnk sandbox tool list [--json]
```

It takes `--json`, boolean: Print the answer as JSON for other programs. It answers `sandbox.tools-listed`.

### `lnk sandbox tool remove`

Remove a tool: no sandbox reaches it anymore

```usage
lnk sandbox tool remove <name>
```

It takes `name`, position 1, string, required: The tool. It answers `sandbox.ended`.
